title: docs: a marketplace handbook for app authors — listing metadata, README conventions, `os package publish --submit`, review, the customer install experience (credentials, sample data, upgrade, uninstall) and staying current with platform versions
body:
**Filing gate ③** (maintainer-directed task). The maintainer in this session, 2026-10-28, verbatim: 「要的，立一张上架手册的卡」, answering the offer of a handbook for third-party app authors covering the whole road from a built artifact to a customer's installed app.

**Filed by** `session_01J8VVAjRKqdoEYQ4hXxtBuf`. ⛔ Not a claim. Lane suggestion: `domain:devx` (`content/docs/**`). Triage sets labels and priority. North Star road step ④ 「发布并装进一个环境」 is the step this page serves; its checklist items are `platform-core.marketplace-install-local-lifecycle`, `platform-core.marketplace-console-honesty`, `platform-core.manifest-install-contract`, `platform-core.package-lifecycle-enable-disable`, `cli.plugin-manifest-build-contract`.

**Business reason.** The North Star's one measure is a new AI developer walking from `npm create objectstack` to an app published and installed into an environment. The mechanics of that step are documented in pieces — `content/docs/deployment/publish-and-preview.mdx` (compile, publish a version, install, preview), `install-modes.mdx`, `app-dependencies.mdx`, `cloud-connection.mdx`, the CLI reference for `os package publish` / `os package install` (#8965) — but no page tells an author **what a marketplace listing is made of and what the customer will go through**: the `objectstack.manifest.json` listing fields (display name, tagline, description, category, icon, screenshots with captions, `translations`), the README conventions a listing relies on (what the app does, what credentials it needs and where to get them — the hand-off ruled on #27230), `--submit` and what review looks at, how the customer's administrator sees the app (Browse Marketplace vs. import of an artifact, the credential prompt, sample data reseed/purge, enable/disable, upgrade by publishing a new version, uninstall and what it removes), and how to stay current with platform versions (`engines.protocol`, `os migrate meta`, why an app pinned to an old platform leaves the catalog). The survey of 2026-10-27 found every downstream app but HotCRM pinned to an older platform — a handbook that says "this is what keeps you listed" is the cheapest countermeasure. Readers: third-party and first-party app authors (HotCRM, HotCLM, hotsrm, ATS, Duly maintainers included), and the agents that write apps from `skills/**`.

**Who acts.** The `domain:devx` seat writes one page (plus `meta.json`), linking the existing deployment pages rather than duplicating them; HotCRM's `README.md` and `objectstack.manifest.json` serve as the worked example. Facts about the hosted review flow that live in the cloud repository are stated only as far as this repository's CLI exposes them (`--submit`, `--auto-approve`, listing status); nothing is asserted about the control plane that the author cannot see from here (Prime Directive #10).

**Dedupe** (semantic issue search, `objectstack-ai/objectstack`, open and closed, 2026-10-28): "docs publish an app to the marketplace install an app guide os package publish install-local hand-written documentation" → 2 hits, both closed and both narrower: #8965 (CLI reference entries for the two commands), #8910 (`publish-and-preview` rewritten to name both ways an app reaches the platform). No handbook card exists.

### Governing text

- **North Star** 「唯一的度量，那条路」: 「发布并装进一个环境」 is step ④; 「写给 AI 的文档与 skills 说错一句，等于产品缺陷」. Re-check: `git grep -n "发布并装进一个环境" origin/main -- docs/NORTH-STAR.md`.
- **ADR-0019 D1/D2**: the listing is an App listing; only `type: app` is consumer-installable. Re-check: `git grep -n "A Marketplace" origin/main -- docs/adr/0019-app-as-consumer-unit.md`.
- **`packages/spec/src/marketplace/template-manifest.zod.ts`** (`objectstack.manifest.json`) and `package.zod.ts` (`translations`: display name, description, readme, tagline, screenshot captions; `isStarter`; visibility). Re-check: `git grep -n "screenshotCaptions\|isStarter" origin/main -- packages/spec/src/marketplace`.
- **ADR-0087**: the protocol handshake at install; **ADR-0141**: declared dependencies checked before install; **ADR-0131 D6**: managed / unmanaged install modes.
- **AGENTS.md Prime Directive #10**: never advertise a capability the runtime does not deliver — the handbook describes only the doors that exist today and names the cards for the ones coming (#27237 / #27238 credential prompt, #26709 normalization).

**Protocol statement.** `Metadata-protocol: none`. Docs only. `Skills-docs: updated here` is satisfied by the page itself; `skills/objectstack-platform` gains one link line to it (governed surface — that one-line edit lands with the maintainer, or is left as a follow-up line in the PR).

### Premises (each with a re-check; read at `c3fb185a`)

1. No hand-written page covers listing metadata or the customer's install experience. Re-check: `git grep -rln -i "screenshot" origin/main -- content/docs --and --not -e references` (expected: no deployment page) and `git grep -n "Browse Marketplace" origin/main -- content/docs` (expected 0 outside releases).
2. The pieces that exist are the five deployment pages named above. Re-check: `ls content/docs/deployment`.
3. HotCRM carries the worked example: `objectstack.manifest.json`, `assets/screenshots/**/meta.yaml`, a README with an "Install from the marketplace" section. Re-check in `objectstack-ai/hotcrm`: `ls assets/screenshots/hotcrm && grep -n "Install from the marketplace" README.md`.

### Work (one PR)

1. **`content/docs/deployment/marketplace-handbook.mdx`** (name per the lane), sections in the order an author meets them:
   - What a listing is (ADR-0019: one App, one listing) and what the catalog shows.
   - The listing file: every `objectstack.manifest.json` field with the HotCRM values as the example; `translations` for zh-CN / en and screenshot captions; the screenshot convention (`assets/screenshots/<screen>/<locale>.png` + `meta.yaml`).
   - README conventions a listing depends on: what the app does in business words, the demo data and demo staff, **the credentials it needs** (name, where to obtain, which permissions) — the author writes names, the administrator supplies values.
   - Build and verify before publishing: `pnpm verify` green, `engines.protocol`, the checklist run record.
   - Publish: `os package publish` flags that matter for a listing (`--display-name`, `--category`, `--icon-file`, `--readme-file`, `--visibility`, `--submit`, `--pre-release`), what review examines, listing statuses.
   - The customer's side, step by step: Browse Marketplace vs. artifact import (`install-local`), install modes, the dependency check, the credential prompt (#27237 / #27238 once landed; until then the env-var path), sample data reseed / purge, enable / disable, upgrade by publishing a new version, uninstall and what it removes — each pointing at the existing page that owns the detail.
   - Staying listed: platform versions, `os migrate meta`, what happens to an app that falls behind.
   - Region packs and modules: dependencies (`app-dependencies.mdx`) and build-time composition, as the two shapes an app can ship extras in.
2. `meta.json` entry; cross-links from `publish-and-preview.mdx` and `getting-started/your-first-project.mdx`.
3. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/docs build` green; `scripts/docs-audit` affected-docs list run on the new page.

### Acceptance

- A reader starting from a built `dist/objectstack.json` can, from this page alone plus the pages it links, produce a listing with icon, screenshots and two locales, publish it, and describe to a customer administrator every screen they will meet from install to uninstall.
- No sentence names a key, flag or screen the runtime at the PR's base does not deliver; forthcoming pieces are named with their card numbers.
- The docs build and link check pass.

### Out of scope

- The hosted review workflow's internals and the publisher dashboard (cloud repository).
- The credential UI itself (#27238) and the normalization tool (#26709); the handbook links them when they land.
